cwg.name: Mozambique Cash and Voucher Working Group (Maputo, with Beira sub-group)
cwg.evidence_note: National group active since 2017, supported by the Southern Africa regional technical CWG; leads and meeting frequency not stated. Monthly partner cash overviews published through Dec 2025 (26 partners, USD 27.9M, 904,000 people).

ai_summary.headline: Mozambique has a large, mostly voucher-based cash response but no MPC line, no pooled fund and a thinly documented CWG.
ai_summary.narrative: Cash is delivered at scale but sits inside sector programming. Partners reported USD 27.9M and 904,000 people reached with cash in 2025, across 26 partners, mostly paper vouchers (67%), with mobile money 19% and e-vouchers 14% [s11]. The 2026 plan is USD 534.3M after a floods addendum and is 43.1% funded [s1], but it carries no Multi Purpose Cash cluster line and the HNRP only says MPC is promoted for efficiency [s4]. There is no country-based pooled fund, so the only humanitarian pooled money is CERF [s6]. Stated preference looks cash-leaning (about 69% physical cash against 65% in-kind in a 2024 national survey), but the label pairing in that source is uncertain and it is not specific to the northern response [s8]. The Maputo CWG exists, though leads and activity level were not found [s10]. Market monitoring appears to lapse: the latest WFP bulletin found is Q2 2025 [s9]. No cost-efficiency or feasibility evidence was located.
barriers: No MPC requirement line in the plan, so MPC funding cannot be tracked in FTS
No country-based pooled fund to channel flexible cash money
Voucher-heavy delivery (paper vouchers 67%) limits flexibility compared with unrestricted cash
Market monitoring outputs found are over 12 months old
CWG leadership and capacity are undocumented publicly
opportunities: 2025 experience points to expanding into MPC in emergencies, and 24-26 partners already deliver cash [s11]
Voucher approaches are aligned with national systems, offering a social protection entry point
data_gaps: current preference survey for the northern response

total_funding_usd.note: All incoming funding to the plan, pledges excluded. Matches the FTS plan summary.

mpc_usd.note: No multi-purpose cash cluster with funding is visible on FTS for this plan (the plan may still carry an MPC requirement), so MPC funding cannot be seen.

ctp_usd.note: All flows tagged 'Cash transfer programming (CTP)', inside or outside the MPC cluster.

sectoral_cva_usd.note: Flows whose FTS modality field is 'Cash transfer programming (CTP)' and whose destination cluster is not multi-purpose cash: 24 flows. The CTP tag is set by the reporting donor or agency and is not applied consistently, so this is a floor, not a measure of sectoral cash. Largest: Food Security and Livelihoods US$5.8M, Shelter/NFIs US$0.3M, Education US$0.1M.

cva_usd.note: Union of the MPC cluster and the CTP tag. Widest defensible FTS cash figure; still a floor because untagged sectoral cash is invisible.

cva_pct_of_total.note: cva_usd as a share of total plan funding.

sectoral_cva_pct_of_total.note: sectoral_cva_usd as a share of total plan funding.

mpc_pct_of_total.note: MPC cluster funding as a share of total plan funding (single-cluster view).

fts_cva.caveat: FTS records funding, not transfers to people, and only to first-level recipients. Sectoral cash depends on a modality tag that reporters apply unevenly.

cva_to_local_pct.note: Indicator 4.2 proxy. Share of FTS cash funding (MPC cluster or CTP tag, US$7.3M) whose first-level recipient is a local or national NGO/CSO or a national government body. FTS does not see sub-grants, so this understates money that reaches local actors through international intermediaries.

all_funding_to_local_pct.note: Share of all plan funding whose first-level recipient is a local or national actor (US$0.0M). Same first-level caveat.

localisation.caveat: FTS sees first-level recipients only; indicator 4.2 as defined (direct donor allocation to local partners) is therefore a floor. Chair roles come from public CWG pages and may be out of date.
